chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Halabi from Ubayd ibn Zurarah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the last two rak'ahs of Dhuhr. He said: 'You glorify (Allah) and praise Allah and seek forgiveness for your sin, and if you wish, [recite] the Opening of the Book, for indeed it is praise and supplication.'

key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ: the Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What should be recited in the last two rak'ahs of Dhuhr prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexible nature of the two sunnah rak'ahs of Dhuhr, emphasizing that the core essence lies in glorification and repentance rather than rigid recitation. The Imam’s option to recite Surah Al-Fatiha highlights its dual role as both *Hamd* (praise) and *Du'a* (supplication), a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the sufficiency of Fatiha in optional prayers. This reflects the broader Shia principle of ease (*yusr*) in worship, allowing the believer to choose between the full recitation or the essential dhikr based on their capacity.
